title: AVWAP Reclaim
teaches: The AVWAP reclaim as we trade it: a stock above its 200-day falls hard from a high everyone can see, closes under the anchored VWAP from that high for weeks until the line flattens, then closes clearly back over it; we buy only after price proves the reclaim, never at the touch, the stop sits a few cents under the reclaim day's low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

questions.q: On a daily chart, what does an AVWAP anchored to a stock's high show?
choices: Volume-weighted cost since the high
The average close of 50 days
The highest price since the anchor
The open price of the anchor day
questions.why: The average price paid since the high, weighted by volume. Typical price times volume, summed from the anchor day, divided by volume.
questions.lesson_line: The AVWAP is the average buyer's cost since one event. Name the event first.

wrong.The average close of 50 days: That is a 50-day moving average. It has no anchor and no volume weight.
wrong.The highest price since the anchor: That is a level, not an average. The AVWAP falls as buyers pay less.
wrong.The open price of the anchor day: The anchor day is where the sum starts. The line moves with every day after it.

questions.q: The AVWAP from a prior high shows whether the average buyer since that high is winning or losing.
questions.why: True. Shannon reads it that way, and ChartSchool says it shows whether bulls or bears have been in charge since a specific time.
questions.lesson_line: Under the line, the average holder since the high is losing. Back over it, they are even again.

questions.q: We take an AVWAP reclaim only when the reclaim day closes above the 200-day SMA.
questions.why: True. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average; the reclaim day's close must sit above it.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day there is no long to take, however clean the line looks.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.why: Flat. Shannon's worked case: buyers regained control as price surged above the flat AVWAP, after the line flattened out.
questions.lesson_line: A falling line is still the sellers' line. Wait for it to flatten.
questions.sentence: Shannon: the buyers had regained control as the price surged above the ___ AVWAP.

questions.q: After the buy, one close back under the AVWAP is an exit by itself.
questions.why: False. A close back under the AVWAP after the buy is not an exit by itself; the stop decides. Shannon weighs the line's direction over a close or two.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the line is a warning. The stop is the exit.

questions.q: Which anchor is one Shannon would call meaningful?
choices: A major high everyone can see
The day you bought the stock
A date that makes the line fit
A random bar from last month
questions.answer: A major high everyone can see
questions.why: A major high everyone can see. He anchors to major highs and lows, big news or strong reversals. TrendSpider warns that picking the anchor is subjective.
questions.lesson_line: Anchor to an event the whole market saw. A date that makes the line fit is not one.

wrong.The day you bought the stock: Your entry is not a market event. Nobody else's cost started there.
wrong.A date that makes the line fit: That is fitting the line to the chart. It tells you nothing about other buyers.
wrong.A random bar from last month: A random bar has no story. The anchor is where price movement began or reversed.

questions.q: On an AVWAP reclaim, the stop goes a few cents under the reclaim day's low.
questions.why: True. A few cents under the day's low, our default stop. That low normally sits at or under the AVWAP, so a stop-out also means the reclaim failed.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the reclaim day's low.

questions.q: By our card, how far over the AVWAP should the reclaim day close?
choices: 0.3 to 1.0 ATR over the line
Anywhere above it, even a cent
At least 2 ATR over the line
Right on the line at the close
questions.why: 0.3 to 1.0 ATR over the line: clear, but not stretched. ATR is the stock's average true range, a typical day's move.
questions.lesson_line: Over the line by a real margin, not a poke, and not a sprint.

wrong.Anywhere above it, even a cent: A close a hair over the line sits inside the noise. The card wants 0.3 ATR at least.
wrong.At least 2 ATR over the line: Past 1.0 ATR is too stretched; the card makes it no trade.
wrong.Right on the line at the close: On the line is not back over it. Nothing is reclaimed yet.

questions.q: A reclaim day that closes mid-range, just over the line, is the A+ version of the reclaim day.
questions.why: False. The A+ cue: the reclaim day closes near its high. A B- version closes mid-range, just over the line.
questions.lesson_line: Where the reclaim day closes in its range grades the day.

questions.q: Shannon reads a gap up over a cluster of AVWAPs as buyers back in control.
questions.why: True. He does. Our card splits it off anyway: a reclaim day that gaps over the line is judged as a gap setup. That split is ours, not his.
questions.lesson_line: A gap over the line is a gap trade for us. Judge it with the gap rules.

questions.q: Our card wants a real fall first: the anchor high minus the lowest low since it is at least 4 ATR.
questions.why: True. A real fall comes first, at least 4 ATR from the high, so there are holders since the high who are losing.
questions.lesson_line: No real fall, no trapped holders. The reclaim needs a fall behind it.

questions.q: Two reclaims, both closing above the 200-day. Which is the better one by our card?
choices: The one over a rising 200-day
The one over a falling 200-day
No difference; above is above
questions.why: The one over a rising 200-day. Better: the 200-day is higher than it was 20 sessions ago.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day is the gate. A rising 200-day is the better version.

wrong.The one over a falling 200-day: A falling 200-day is a weaker trend under the trade. The card prefers rising.
wrong.No difference; above is above: Above is the gate. Rising is the grade on top of it.

questions.q: Skip an AVWAP reclaim long that is more than 10% above its 10-day average.
questions.why: True. Too stretched to buy: skip a long that is more than 10% above its 10-day average.
questions.lesson_line: A reclaim that already ran is a chase with a new name.

questions.q: The market reading is Red and a clean AVWAP reclaim triggers. Your call?
choices: No new long
Buy full size; it is clean
Buy half size
Buy only if volume is heavy
questions.why: No new long. Our card: Red, no new longs. The rulebook says Red is mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: A clean reclaim in a Red market is still a long in a Red market.

wrong.Buy full size; it is clean: Clean is the chart. Red is the market, and Red says no new longs.
wrong.Buy half size: Size does not fix the reading. Red is no new longs.
wrong.Buy only if volume is heavy: Volume does not override the market reading.

questions.q: Our stop on an AVWAP reclaim is the AVWAP minus half an ATR.
questions.why: False. That is the scanner's stop, and no source has it. Ours is a few cents under the reclaim day's low.
questions.lesson_line: The day's low is the stop. The line is the idea, not the stop.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.why: 4%. No buy more than 4% above the trigger. Past it, the stop is too far away and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent past the trigger and I let it go.
questions.sentence: Never buy an AVWAP reclaim more than ___% above the trigger.

questions.q: A stock closes back over a line that starts at its March high and bends with volume. Which setup?
choices: An AVWAP reclaim
A Remount of a moving average
A U&R of a prior low
questions.why: An AVWAP reclaim. A line that starts at an event day and bends with volume is the AVWAP. A Remount takes back a moving average or a flat level.
questions.lesson_line: Name the line. An event and volume make it an AVWAP.

wrong.A Remount of a moving average: A moving average has no anchor day. This line starts at the March high.
wrong.A U&R of a prior low: A U&R undercuts a prior low. This is a line taken back from below.

questions.q: Our AVWAP, computed from daily bars, is exact, the same as the intraday line.
questions.why: False. It is an approximation of the intraday line. Shannon wants the shortest timeframe for the most accurate measure.
questions.lesson_line: The daily line is close, not exact. Read it as a zone.

questions.q: Bought at 17.70 with the stop at 17.50. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 18.30. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. NOW got there in five sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Know 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: The AVWAP from the high is reclaimed, but the IPO-high AVWAP sits 3% overhead. Grade?
choices: B-: a line just overhead
A+: the reclaim is clean
No trade: never with a line above
questions.why: B-. Another AVWAP within a few percent overhead is the B- cue. Clear air to the next line is the A+.
questions.lesson_line: Look up before you buy. The next line is where it meets supply.

wrong.A+: the reclaim is clean: The reclaim can be clean and still have a ceiling 3% away. That grades it down.
wrong.No trade: never with a line above: Overhead is a grade cue, not a gate. CAT paused under the 50-day overhead and then ran.

questions.q: No new AVWAP reclaim buy in the 3 sessions before an earnings report.
questions.why: True. No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report.
questions.lesson_line: Check the calendar before the chart.

questions.q: AVWAP reclaim or U&R?
questions.story: A stock held above a rising AVWAP for months. Tuesday it dips under the line. Thursday it closes back over.
choices: A U&R-style shakeout
An AVWAP reclaim
Neither; it is broken
questions.why: A U&R-style shakeout. It closed back over within days of a dip under a line it had held. Our reclaim comes after weeks under a line that has flattened.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes under the line. Days is a shakeout; weeks is a reclaim.

wrong.An AVWAP reclaim: A reclaim needs a long stay under a falling line. Two days under a rising line is not that.
wrong.Neither; it is broken: A quick dip and a close back over is a shakeout, not a break.

questions.q: Buy the touch?
questions.story: A stock has closed under its AVWAP from the high for weeks. This morning it rallies up and touches the line from below.
choices: No; wait for proof of a reclaim
Yes; the line is support there
Yes, with a stop under the AVWAP
questions.answer: No; wait for proof of a reclaim
questions.why: No. The line is a level of interest, not a place to do business. Buying the touch instead of the proof is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Don't buy the dip. Buy strength after it.

wrong.Yes; the line is support there: From below, the line is overhead. It has to be taken back first.
wrong.Yes, with a stop under the AVWAP: A stop at a line you have not reclaimed is a guess, and the touch is not a trigger.

questions.q: The last third of an AVWAP reclaim winner trails the 10-day or 21-day and is sold the moment price touches it.
questions.why: False. Default trail: the 10-day for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones; sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the rising average. Sell the close below it.

questions.q: Anchor high 60.00, lowest low since 51.00, ATR 1.80. How many ATR did it fall?
questions.why: 5 ATR. The high minus the lowest low, divided by the ATR. That clears the card's 4 ATR, so it counts as a real fall.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the fall in ATR, not in dollars.

questions.q: AVWAP 45.20, ATR 1.10, the reclaim day closes 46.55. How far over the line, in ATR?
questions.why: 1.23 ATR. The close minus the line, divided by the ATR. That is past the card's 1.0 ATR: too stretched, no trade.
questions.lesson_line: Clear the line, but do not sprint past it.

questions.q: Fill 22.93. The reclaim day's low is 22.71 and the stop sits three cents under it. How far is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 1.09%. A few cents under the reclaim day's low, well inside the 3% the stop usually sits within. That was MAR's stop, 22.68.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: Account 100,000. Risk 0.5%. Fill 120.84, stop 118.83. How many shares?
questions.why: 248. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size, never the other way round.

questions.q: Sell, or hold to the stop?
questions.story: You bought at 52.41 with the stop at 50.95. Day three closes at 51.40, back under the AVWAP but above your stop.
choices: Hold; the stop decides
Sell at the close
Move the stop under the AVWAP
Add; it is cheaper
questions.why: Hold. After the buy, a close back under the AVWAP is not an exit by itself; the stop decides. The stop only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the line is a warning. The order with the broker is the decision.

wrong.Sell at the close: That is the scanner's exit, with no source. Our exit is the stop.
wrong.Move the stop under the AVWAP: The stop is already set from the reclaim day's low. It only ever moves up.
wrong.Add; it is cheaper: Full size at one price with one stop; no adding.

questions.q: Buy or pass?
questions.story: Your trigger is 50.00. You missed the open, and at 10:20 the stock trades 52.40.
choices: Pass; over 4% past the trigger
Buy; the reclaim is confirmed
Buy half size to limit the risk
Buy it with a wider stop to fit
questions.why: Pass. 52.40 is more than 4% over 50.00. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put, so the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: I would rather miss it than chase it.

wrong.Buy; the reclaim is confirmed: Confirmed and too far away are both true. The line is 4%.
wrong.Buy half size to limit the risk: Half of a chased entry is still a chased entry.
wrong.Buy it with a wider stop to fit: A wider stop to fit a late entry is the mistake, not the fix.

questions.q: Where is the stop now?
questions.story: You bought at 50.00 with the stop at 49.00. It gaps open at 48.70, under your stop. The first 30-minute bar's low is 48.40.
choices: 48.40, the first 30-minute low
Sell at the open, 48.70
No stop until it regains 49.00
Out; the loss is past 2R
questions.why: 48.40. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low. That low is inside the 2R ceiling, so it is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the one exception. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Sell at the open, 48.70: The gap rule gives it the first 30 minutes. The 30-minute low is the decision.
wrong.No stop until it regains 49.00: There is always a stop. The new one is the 30-minute low.
wrong.Out; the loss is past 2R: The loss from 50.00 to 48.40 stays inside the 2R ceiling.

questions.q: The 10-day average is 40.00 and the stock trades 44.80 at the trigger. How far above the 10-day, in percent?
questions.why: 12%. Past the 10% line: too stretched to buy, so skip it.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stretch from the 10-day before you buy.

questions.q: Keep the alert?
questions.story: The reclaim day closed 0.6 ATR over the line. The next day never clears its high and closes back under the AVWAP.
choices: No; a close back under ends it
Yes; keep it, set a cent higher
Yes; buy the next close over it
questions.answer: No; a close back under ends it
questions.why: No. A close back at or under the AVWAP before the trigger trades is no trade. Shannon: don't hold and hope.
questions.lesson_line: The reclaim has to hold until the buy. If it slips back first, walk away.

wrong.Yes; keep it, set a cent higher: The level is not the problem. The close back under ended the setup.
wrong.Yes; buy the next close over it: A new close over is a new reclaim, judged from scratch. This one is off.

questions.q: After the buy, an AVWAP reclaim that trades down to the stop is sold at the stop.
questions.why: True. The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. Shannon: don't hold and hope.
questions.lesson_line: My stop is my stop. That is the whole rule.

questions.q: How does that grade the reclaim in your list?
questions.story: A correction just ended. Four software names reclaim their AVWAPs from their highs in the same week, yours among them.
choices: Up: the group is moving together
Down: too crowded
No change; only the chart counts
questions.answer: Up: the group is moving together
questions.why: Up. Several stocks in one group reclaiming together is a grade marker, best after a correction ends.
questions.lesson_line: One reclaim is a stock. Several in one group is a move.

wrong.Down: too crowded: A group moving together is support for each name, not crowding.
wrong.No change; only the chart counts: The card makes the group a grade marker. It counts.

questions.q: What did the stop do?
questions.story: A 7.6 ATR fall, 47 closes under, a flat line. You bought at 262.81, stop 255.97. Day 2 takes the stop. Its low over the next twenty sessions is 12.7% under your buy.
choices: Its job: a planned 1R loss
Cost you; it needed room
Nothing; the line was the exit
questions.why: Its job. Everything in the picture was right and the reclaim still failed; the stop said so. Holding to that low would have cost about five times as much.
questions.lesson_line: A loss taken at plan is the system working.

wrong.Cost you; it needed room: Room was a 12.7% hole. The stop saved most of it.
wrong.Nothing; the line was the exit: The close under the line is a warning. The stop is the exit, and it was.

questions.q: Buy again?
questions.story: You were stopped out the day after you bought. Weeks later the stock has held the line and triggers again.
choices: Yes, as a new trade, new stop
No; one try per line, no more
Yes, but with a wider stop
questions.answer: Yes, as a new trade, new stop
questions.why: Yes. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule. At most 3 tries in a week.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a verdict on the level. The next trigger is a new trade.

wrong.No; one try per line, no more: The limit is 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month, not one.
wrong.Yes, but with a wider stop: The stop is the day's low again. Widening it to avoid a repeat is the mistake.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
questions.story: Your AVWAP long closed Thursday at 2.7R. Friday it gaps open at 3.3R.
choices: Sell a third at the open
Wait for the close
Sell everything
Raise the stop and hold all
questions.answer: Sell a third at the open
questions.why: Sell a third at the open. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through a trim level is the trim. Take it.

wrong.Wait for the close: The level is already passed. Waiting gives the gap a chance to fill.
wrong.Sell everything: A third at 3R. The rest waits for 5R and the trail.
wrong.Raise the stop and hold all: The stop can rise too, but the trim is the rule at the open.

questions.q: An AVWAP reclaim gets 20 trading days to get past 1R before it is sold.
questions.why: False. Time stop: a trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and nothing. The money has somewhere better to be.

questions.q: When does the stop move to breakeven on an AVWAP reclaim winner?
choices: Between 2R and 5R, often at a trim
The day after entry, to be safe
Never; the stop stays where it is
As soon as it closes over the line
questions.answer: Between 2R and 5R, often at a trim
questions.why: Between 2R and 5R, ideally. The first trim at 3R is the natural moment.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven between 2R and 5R. Earlier is noise.

wrong.The day after entry, to be safe: That sits inside the noise. A normal day would take it.
wrong.Never; the stop stays where it is: The stop only moves up. Up to breakeven is allowed.
wrong.As soon as it closes over the line: Every reclaim closes over the line. That is the setup, not the profit.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: The reclaim triggers. The reclaim day's low sits 4.1% under your fill, wider than your usual stop.
choices: Size down from it, or skip
Pull the stop up to 3%
Use the AVWAP as the stop
questions.answer: Size down from it, or skip
questions.why: Size down from the honest stop, or skip if it does not fit the risk. Never tighten it into the noise to make it fit.
questions.lesson_line: You never pick a size and back-fit a stop.

wrong.Pull the stop up to 3%: That is tightening into the noise to fit the size. The card says never.
wrong.Use the AVWAP as the stop: The line is not the stop. The reclaim day's low is.

questions.q: In our scan, reclaim days on the loudest volume reached 3R more often than quiet ones.
questions.why: False. The loudest days reached 3R 22.3% of the time; the quietest, 27.0%. Loud volume did not help.
questions.lesson_line: Volume did not sort the winners here. The stop and the market did more.

questions.q: What changes on your next AVWAP reclaim?
questions.story: Bought at 43.22, stop 42.43. The next session takes the stop. The next 10 closes are all back under the line. Its low over the next twenty sessions is 11.6% under your buy.
choices: Nothing; same stop, same rules
Widen the stop next time
Stop trading reclaims
Buy the dip under the line
questions.why: Nothing. You followed every rule and the reclaim failed. The stop cost 1R; holding to that low would have cost many times that.
questions.lesson_line: You will take this loss again. It is the price of the ones that run.

wrong.Widen the stop next time: A wider stop here would have ridden it down 11.6%. The stop worked.
wrong.Stop trading reclaims: One planned loss is not a verdict on the setup.
wrong.Buy the dip under the line: That is averaging into a failed reclaim. The stop is the exit.

questions.q: Take it by our card?
questions.story: Price closes back over the AVWAP from a September high. Over the last 10 sessions that line still fell 0.56 ATR.
choices: No; the line had not flattened
Yes; it closed over the line
Yes; a steep line breaks harder
questions.answer: No; the line had not flattened
questions.why: No. The line still fell 0.56 ATR in 10 sessions; the card wants under 0.5. It reached 9.3R anyway: the rule is a quality filter, not a prediction.
questions.lesson_line: A move above a declining line will often fail. Wait for it to flatten.

wrong.Yes; it closed over the line: The close is one gate. The flattened line is another, and this fails it.
wrong.Yes; a steep line breaks harder: Shannon says the steeper the angle, the likelier the move across fails.

questions.q: Does it qualify as an AVWAP reclaim?
questions.story: A stock dips 3.9 ATR from a one-month high, closes under the AVWAP from that high 19 times, then closes back over.
choices: No; not a real fall
Yes; it closed back over
Yes; 19 closes under is enough
questions.why: No. 3.9 ATR is short of the 4 the card wants: a dip from a one-month high, not a real fall. It reached 6.4R; the rule still rejects it.
questions.lesson_line: Near enough is not a rule. The fall is a gate.

wrong.Yes; it closed back over: The close over is the last step. The fall behind it has to be real first.
wrong.Yes; 19 closes under is enough: Time under is one test. The fall is another, and this one fails it.

questions.q: What is the read on that reclaim day?
questions.story: After weeks under a flat AVWAP, the stock closes 0.23 ATR over it.
choices: A poke inside the noise; pass
A clean reclaim; buy tomorrow
A gap setup instead
questions.answer: A poke inside the noise; pass
questions.why: A poke. 0.23 ATR is under the card's 0.3 to 1.0 ATR. It chopped to 2.7R before a gap did the real work.
questions.lesson_line: A hair over the line is still the line. Clear it.

wrong.A clean reclaim; buy tomorrow: Clean starts at 0.3 ATR over the line. This is inside the noise.
wrong.A gap setup instead: Nothing gapped. It closed barely over the line.

questions.q: Which setup is it?
questions.story: After weeks under the AVWAP from its high, a stock opens 0.91 ATR above the line and closes higher.
choices: A gap setup, not a reclaim
A clean reclaim from below
A U&R of the AVWAP line
questions.answer: A gap setup, not a reclaim
questions.why: A gap setup. It opened 0.91 ATR over the line, past the card's 0.5, so the line was never retaken from below in regular hours.
questions.lesson_line: Look at the open. A gap over the line is judged as a gap.

wrong.A clean reclaim from below: The reclaim is taken back from below during the day. This one gapped over.
wrong.A U&R of the AVWAP line: A U&R dips under a level and comes back. This gapped over a line it was under.

questions.q: The stock trades 3,000,000 shares a day on average. Our ceiling on the position?
choices: 30,000 shares, 1% of daily volume
300,000 shares, a tenth of volume
No ceiling if the stop is tight
3,000 shares, a tenth of the cap
questions.why: 30,000 shares. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.
questions.lesson_line: One percent of the daily volume, and not a share more.

wrong.300,000 shares, a tenth of volume: That is a tenth of the day's volume. You could not get out without moving it.
wrong.No ceiling if the stop is tight: A tight stop cannot catch an overnight gap. The ceiling stands.
wrong.3,000 shares, a tenth of the cap: That is a tenth of the 1% ceiling. The ceiling is 1%, not less.

questions.q: On our card, the index sitting above its AVWAP from its last major low grades a reclaim up.
questions.why: True. The index above its AVWAP from the most recent major low or follow-through day is a grade cue on the card.
questions.lesson_line: Read the index's own line before the stock's.

questions.q: Take the reclaim?
questions.story: A clean reclaim on an $8 stock that trades about $5 million a day.
choices: No; under $10 and $20M a day
Yes; the line is clean
Yes, at half size to be safe
questions.why: No. Only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. Thin stocks also distort the AVWAP itself.
questions.lesson_line: A clean line in a thin stock is still a thin stock.

wrong.Yes; the line is clean: The line is fine and the stock is not ours. Liquidity comes before the chart.
wrong.Yes, at half size to be safe: Size does not make a thin stock liquid.

questions.q: Which setup is it?
questions.story: After an earnings gap up, a stock pulls back to the gap day's low from above, holds it and closes in the upper half.
choices: Gap Support, a hold from above
A reclaim after weeks under
A Kicker over a red day's high
questions.answer: Gap Support, a hold from above
questions.why: Gap Support. It held the gap-up day's low from above. The earnings AVWAP reclaim buys the first close back over the line from below, after weeks under it.
questions.lesson_line: Above the line and holding is Gap Support. Back over it from below is the reclaim.

wrong.A reclaim after weeks under: A reclaim comes from below after weeks under the line. This never went under.
wrong.A Kicker over a red day's high: A Kicker gaps up through a red day's high. This is a test that holds.

questions.q: The typical price behind our AVWAP is the average of the day's open, high and low.
questions.why: False. Typical price is the average of the day's high, low and close. ChartSchool's formula, the one our card uses: typical price times volume, summed from the anchor day, divided by volume.
questions.lesson_line: High, low and close, averaged, weighted by volume, summed from the anchor.

questions.q: Shannon, the source we follow, calls a breakout above the AVWAP a mechanical signal to buy.
questions.why: False. Shannon calls the AVWAP a place to look for evidence, not a mechanical signal. TrendSpider is the one that calls a breakout above the line a signal to go long.
questions.lesson_line: The line is where to look for evidence, not what to do.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: In the last month the stock closed over its AVWAP, back under, over again and under again. Today it closes 0.5 ATR over.
choices: Pass; chop, too many crossings
Buy; it closed clearly over it
Buy; the line is well tested
questions.why: Pass. More than 2 crossings in the 30 sessions before is chop, not a first reclaim. Shannon: oscillating above and below indicates indecision.
questions.lesson_line: Many crossings mean nobody is in control. Wait for the first clean one.

wrong.Buy; it closed clearly over it: Clearly over for the third time in a month is a poke in a chop.
wrong.Buy; the line is well tested: Crossings back and forth are indecision, not a tested ceiling.

questions.q: What did the scan not see?
questions.story: A 9.6 ATR fall, then a reclaim close 0.78 ATR over the line on 1.54x volume. It is stopped with 0.0R. The broad market fell that year.
choices: The market falling under it
Too little volume
A gap over the line
questions.why: The market. A clean-looking reclaim in a year the broad market fell, stopped with 0.0R. The index's own standing matters.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market before the line.

wrong.Too little volume: Volume was heavy, 1.54x. It did not help.
wrong.A gap over the line: Nothing in the story gapped. The miss was the market.

questions.q: What protects the last third?
questions.story: Your reclaim reached 5R and you took both trims. Then a market crash starts and the stock is heading for half its price.
choices: The trail: out on a close below it
The original stop
Nothing; hold for the rebound
questions.answer: The trail: out on a close below it
questions.why: The trail. After a third at 3R and a third at 5R, the last third trails the 10-day or 21-day and goes on a close below.
questions.lesson_line: Two thirds banked and a trail on the rest. That is what survives a crash.

wrong.The original stop: By now the stop sits at breakeven. The trail is the exit that follows the price up.
wrong.Nothing; hold for the rebound: Hope is not a stop. The trail is the exit for the last third.

questions.q: Bought at 52.67, stop 51.99. You sell a third at 56.07. How many R did that third bank?
questions.why: 5R. The gain divided by the fill minus the stop. That is the second trim. EPC reached 3R in six sessions and ran to 18.9R.
questions.lesson_line: Count every exit in R. The second third is 5R.

questions.q: How does that grade the reclaim?
questions.story: After a 19.2% fall the AVWAP flattens near 70. The reclaim day, the 50-day and the trigger all sit within one ATR.
choices: Up: the line sits at a second level
Down; too many lines in one place
No change; the 50-day is not part of it
questions.answer: Up: the line sits at a second level
questions.why: Up. The AVWAP at a second level, here the 50-day, is the A+ cue. Shannon: it's more likely when we have that confluence.
questions.lesson_line: One line is a level. Two lines in one place is a shelf.

wrong.Down; too many lines in one place: Converging lines mark a stronger area, ChartSchool says, not a weaker one.
wrong.No change; the 50-day is not part of it: The card names the 50-day as the second level that grades it up.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: A clean reclaim from a high triggers. The company's earnings reaction day is two sessions away.
choices: No; earnings in two sessions
Yes; the reclaim is clean
Yes, half size
questions.why: No. The buy would come two sessions before the earnings reaction day, inside the 3 days the rule forbids. CDW in 2019 ran 22.4R from that spot, and it is still a pass.
questions.lesson_line: A winner the rules forbid is still a pass. Next time it may be a gap down.

wrong.Yes; the reclaim is clean: Clean is the chart. The calendar still says no.
wrong.Yes, half size: Size does not fix a report risk.

questions.q: In our scan, reclaims with stops over 3% reached 3R more often than tighter ones.
questions.why: False. Stops over 3% reached 3R 22.5% of the time against 29.3% for 2-3% stops, so less often. The 3% line earns its place.
questions.lesson_line: A tight, honest stop is part of the edge, not just the risk.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: The market reading is Orange. A reclaim triggers with another AVWAP 3% overhead.
choices: No; Orange is A+ only
Yes, at full size
Yes; Orange means half size
questions.why: No. Orange is A+ setups only, and a line 3% overhead grades this B-.
questions.lesson_line: Orange narrows you to the best. A B- reclaim waits.

wrong.Yes, at full size: Full risk is Green. Orange is A+ only.
wrong.Yes; Orange means half size: Orange is about grade, not size. A B- stays on the bench.

questions.q: An A+ AVWAP reclaim in a Green market. The risk on the trade?
choices: 1% to 1.5% of the account
0.25% to 0.5% of the account
5% of the account
Whatever fits the stop
questions.why: 1% to 1.5%. Risk by grade: A+ 1% to 1.5%; A and B 0.5% to 1%; B- or lower 0.25% to 0.5%.
questions.lesson_line: The grade sets the risk. The stop turns it into shares.

wrong.0.25% to 0.5% of the account: That is the B- or lower size. A+ is sized up.
wrong.5% of the account: Far past every grade. The grades top out at 1.5%.
wrong.Whatever fits the stop: The stop sets the shares, not the risk. The grade sets the risk.

questions.q: When price reclaims the AVWAP from a high, the average holder since that high is back to even.
questions.why: True. Shannon: when they move back into a winning position, buyers are in control. Name the anchor; a line from a low tells another story.
questions.lesson_line: Every AVWAP tells one group's story. Say which group.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
questions.story: NOW, April 2017. Above a rising 200-day, the line flat, a close 0.31 ATR over it. The reclaim day's high is 17.68 and its low is 17.53. Next session it opens over that high, at 17.70.
choices: Market 17.70; stop 17.50; third at 3R
Limit at the AVWAP; stop 5% under
Market at the close; stop at the line
questions.why: Market at 17.70, stop a few cents under the reclaim day's low at 17.50, a third at 3R. NOW reached 3R in five sessions, before its report.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open.

wrong.Limit at the AVWAP; stop 5% under: Buying the line is buying the touch, and 5% under is nowhere near the day's low.
wrong.Market at the close; stop at the line: The line is not the stop. The reclaim day's low is.

questions.q: How many reclaims do you take this week?
questions.story: A correction ended and the reading just turned Green. Seven leaders on your list are reclaiming their AVWAPs from their highs.
choices: A few; add as they start to work
All seven; Green means full risk
None; wait a month after the turn
questions.answer: A few; add as they start to work
questions.why: A few. After a correction, when the reading turns Green again, start with a few positions. Add more only as the first ones work.
questions.lesson_line: Green after a correction: a few first. Let the winners earn the next ones.

wrong.All seven; Green means full risk: Full risk is the ceiling, not the first day's order. Earn it.
wrong.None; wait a month after the turn: A month after the turn is how you miss the first leg. A few is the rule.

questions.q: Does the 200-day rule keep you out?
questions.story: During the fall, the October low undercut the 200-day. Now, weeks later, the reclaim day closes over the AVWAP and above the 200-day.
choices: No; the reclaim-day close is above it
Yes; it traded under the 200-day
Yes; it must never touch the 200-day
questions.answer: No; the reclaim-day close is above it
questions.why: No. The rule reads the close on the reclaim day. An undercut weeks earlier does not decide it; the close above the 200-day today does.
questions.lesson_line: Read the rule as written: the close on the reclaim day.

wrong.Yes; it traded under the 200-day: The rule is about the close on the reclaim day, not every low before it.
wrong.Yes; it must never touch the 200-day: Touching it in the fall is history. The gate is today's close.

questions.q: What do you tell yourself about the volume?
questions.story: Two reclaims trigger the same day. One came on 2.5x volume, the other on 0.6x. Both pass every gate on the card.
choices: Volume did not sort winners here
Only take the 2.5x one
Only take the 0.6x one
questions.answer: Volume did not sort winners here
questions.why: Volume did not sort winners here. In our scan the loudest reclaim days reached 3R less often than the quiet ones; the stop and the market did more.
questions.lesson_line: A loud reclaim day feels like proof. In our data it was not.

wrong.Only take the 2.5x one: Our scan found loud volume did not help. It is not a reason to drop the other.
wrong.Only take the 0.6x one: Quiet days did a little better, but no rule makes quiet a gate.
